MORROW / WORKLAB Executive summary 3 / 9 Four findings from the workforce Access has spread faster than the practices that turn AI into dependable value. 01 Use is common Regular adoption now reaches most office-based roles. 02 Frontline use trails Access and time remain uneven across roles. 03 Training is thin Many employees learn through trial and error. 04 Workflows lag Most teams add tools before changing the work. MORROW WORKLAB / FICTIONAL RESEARCH DEMO Illustrative findings 3 3 Four findings from the workforce

MORROW / WORKLAB Adoption by role 4 / 9 Adoption is high, but frontline use has stalled Regular AI use rises with seniority, leaving the employees closest to daily operations behind. MORROW / WORKLAB Reported impact 5 / 9 Time savings depend on the work Employees report the largest gains in repeatable administrative tasks and the smallest gains in professional development. Admin 61% Analysis 55% Writing 48% Strategy 37% Learning 29% Illustrative share reporting at least one hour saved on days they use AI, percent illustrative share saving more than one hour 46% MORROW WORKLAB / FICTIONAL RESEARCH DEMO Illustrative survey data 5 5 Time savings depend on the work

MORROW / WORKLAB Adoption barriers 6 / 9 Three barriers shape adoption Employees need practical instruction, approved tools, and visible support from leaders. 01 38% lack practical training Short sessions explain the tool but rarely change the work. 02 34% lack approved tools Employees turn to unsanctioned options when access is limited. 03 27% lack leadership support Teams hesitate when expectations and accountability stay unclear. MORROW WORKLAB / FICTIONAL RESEARCH DEMO Illustrative survey data 6 6 Three barriers shape adoption

MORROW / WORKLAB Operating model 7 / 9 Workflow redesign remains uneven Most companies deploy AI inside existing processes. Fewer reshape the work or invent a different model. deploy AI in existing workflows 68% reshape end-to-end processes 47% invent new operating models 19% MORROW WORKLAB / FICTIONAL RESEARCH DEMO Illustrative survey data; categories may overlap 7 7 Workflow redesign remains uneven

MORROW / WORKLAB AI agents 8 / 9 see meaningful potential 74% 01 31% understand agents Practical familiarity remains much lower than interest. 02 42% worry about oversight Another 35% cite unclear accountability when mistakes occur. AI agents show promise, but understanding remains low Interest is broad. Familiarity with governance, limits, and day-to-day use remains narrow. MORROW WORKLAB / FICTIONAL RESEARCH DEMO Illustrative survey data 8 8 AI agents show promise, but understanding remains low

MORROW / WORKLAB Leadership agenda 9 / 9 Four priorities for leaders The next phase depends on practical capability and deliberate workflow choices. 01 Train for the work Teach employees inside real tasks and decisions. 02 Measure value Track time, quality, satisfaction, and risk. 03 Redesign workflows Change the process when tools alone stop helping. 04 Test agents carefully Define oversight before expanding autonomy.
